topic: Proliferate: Self-Hostable Open-Source Codex for Any Coding Agent

key_points: Open-source (AGPL-3.0) AI IDE by YC S25 founder Pablo; runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, and Grok in parallel in one workspace
Each task gets an isolated git worktree for its branch, terminal, conversation, and review state
Native harnesses preserve each agent's native inference/config options including Bedrock, Azure, and self-hosted inference
Inter-agent communication: a parent agent can spawn and communicate with another supported agent as a subagent
Workflows feature: reusable chains of agent sessions and human approval gates, with harness and model chosen per step
Full control plane is self-hostable via Docker Compose (Caddy, Postgres, API), AWS one-click CloudFormation, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, and air-gapped operation
Orchestrate multiple coding agents from desktop and mobile; ~15k stars
Positioned as the easy-to-set-up alternative; HN commenters praised Paseo's clear docs and quick setup vs Proliferate's confusing docs
Cross-device control (PC to Mac/iPhone) was a pain point where Paseo won in HN feedback
Open-source alternative to Cursor/Codex-style coding agents; ~20k stars, MIT license
Frequently compared to Proliferate in HN discussion as a lighter-weight option
Focuses on a single-agent desktop experience rather than multi-agent orchestration
The dominant open-source autonomous coding agent platform, but heavier and more platform-centric than a self-hostable IDE
Represents the 'platform' end of the spectrum vs Proliferate's 'IDE/harness' approach
Powerful AI coding agent built for the terminal; ~13.7k stars, Go, MIT
HN commenters noted opencode already covers basically every model and provider, questioning the need for another layer on top
Terminal-first, single-agent focus vs Proliferate's multi-agent desktop IDE

stats.fact: Proliferate is open-source under AGPL-3.0, ~404 GitHub stars and 66 forks as of 2026-08-25
Proliferate Show HN post reached 45 points on Hacker News (2026-08-21)
Proliferate supports Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, and Grok through native harnesses, including Bedrock, Azure, and self-hosted inference
Proliferate is a Y Combinator S25 company founded by Pablo
Competitor Paseo has ~15k GitHub stars; t3code ~20k; OpenHands ~85k; OpenCode ~13.7k
Proliferate self-hosting options include Docker Compose (Caddy, Postgres, API), AWS one-click CloudFormation on EC2, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, and air-gapped operation

angles: The 'everything app' thesis: OpenAI wants Codex to be the main interface for getting work done, and Proliferate is the open-source, self-hostable version that preserves optionality across labs and model providers
Multi-agent orchestration as the differentiator: parent agents spawning subagents across different harnesses (e.g., Fable delegating to Codex, OpenCode reviewing PRs) — not just a single-agent IDE
Self-hosting and data control: full control plane self-hostable (Docker, AWS, air-gapped) for teams that don't want to depend on OpenAI or any single vendor
The Workflows feature as the automation moat: reusable chains of agent sessions with human approval gates, harness/model chosen per step
The setup-friction tradeoff: HN feedback shows Proliferate's docs are confusing and setup frustrating vs Paseo's ease — a real adoption barrier to address
Open-weight model support: run agents with open-weight models and self-hosted inference, avoiding vendor lock-in
